activity_context.topic_title: Estimating Derivatives Using a Backward Difference Quotient

feedback.problem:
A function $f(x)$ has values according to the table below:

| $x$ | $-0.5$ | $-0.25$ | $0$ | $0.25$ | $0.5$ | $0.75$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $10$ | $9$ | $8$ | $6$ | $5$ | $3$ |

Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=0.75$ using a backward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

$\,\,{f}^{′}(0.75)≈$ {{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x)-f(x-h)}{h}
$$

 

at the point $x=0.75.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case, $h=0.25.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(0.75) & ≈\frac{f(0.75)-f(0.75-0.25)}{0.25} \\  & =\frac{f(0.75)-f(0.5)}{0.25} \\  & =\frac{3-5}{0.25} \\  & =\frac{-2}{0.25} \\  & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$
